fields.v: Five architecture specification formats (no SDD tool): (1) Prose (control); (2) Mermaid diagrams + numbered constraints + ADRs + route table; (3) OpenAPI 3.0 + Mermaid + constraints; (4) C4 / Structurizr DSL + Mermaid container diagram + constraints + ADRs; (5) TypeScript interface contracts + ArchUnit-style rules (pseudo-code). Baseline: requirements only, no architecture (Sonnet 4.6 only). Versions: OpenAPI 3.0; others Not stated

One architecture specification document per format, all encoding the same 7 elements: 7 components, communication patterns (event bus pub/sub), data ownership, 6 behavioral constraints, 25 HTTP routes, 3 ADRs (design rationale), prescribed file structure. Format-specific artefacts as listed under Approach

Single multi-turn session per trial: agent receives the specification and an identical implementation prompt, then iteratively writes files, compiles (tsc), fixes errors, runs a demo, signals done. No separate spec/plan/tasks phases
None during trials (autonomous agent; specifications authored by the author beforehand and reviewed for information equivalence)
Specification format only (architecture spec given as static context to a custom agent harness)

Not classifiable (no SDD workflow: a human-authored architecture specification is given once as static context before generation and not maintained; closest to spec-first). Authors' wording: 'architecture specification', 'specification as implementation interface', specs should be 'compilable, not merely parseable'
fields.why: The draft gave no level. The study only varies the format of a context document, so 'not classifiable' fits; a reader could call it spec-first since the specification precedes and drives generation

LLM-judge scores 1-10 (Sonnet 4.6, blind to format): architectural adherence, completeness, code quality, constraint compliance, overall; automated constraint violations (static import analysis); weighted architecture compliance score (components 20%, communication 20%, constraints 20%, routes 20%, data ownership 10%, file structure 10%; ~80% of the architecture machine-verifiable); LOC

Process metrics: tsc attempts and pass rate, demo run rate (self-validation), tool-call errors, file rewrite rate (debugging intensity); failure-mode taxonomy (compilation death spiral, premature termination, perfectionist iteration); judge-automation correlation, inter-judge agreement (GPT-5 re-judging), same-family bias

Automatic: harness logs (tokens, turns, tsc, demo, writes), static import analysis, route coverage script. LLM-as-judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6) for the four quality dimensions; 30 trials re-judged by GPT-5. No human scoring

Agent = custom TypeScript harness (tools write_file, read_file, list_files, run_command, done; max 50 turns, 16,384 output tokens/turn, default temperature) for all. Criterion: judge overall (1-10), route coverage, compliance; 3 trials per cell. Values: overall (Table V); route %/compliance % (Table VIII); tokens mean (Table III for Sonnet; Haiku computed from Table IV). Draft verdict rule: quality works = overall >= 8 and route 100%; partly = 6-8; does not work = < 6 or route < 70%. Cost verdicts only where per-cell tokens are reported.

fields.v: Task: one reference system (Task Management API). Configurations: 5 formats x 6 models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5; GPT-5, GPT-5-mini; Gemini 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash) = 30 cells, 90 trials, run as six sequential rounds; plus no-architecture baseline (Sonnet, 3 trials). Baseline: prose (control) for format; requirements-only for the premise. Held constant: information content of specs, implementation prompt, harness and tools, max turns/tokens, default temperature, clean directory, judge model (Sonnet 4.6). Acceptance tests: none functional; route coverage, static compliance and LLM judge. Repetitions: 3 per cell. Human intervention: none

Format x model interaction: format spread (max-min overall) Sonnet 0.17, GPT-5 0.92, GPT-5-mini 0.83, Haiku 1.67, Gemini Flash 1.08, Gemini Pro 2.42 (driven by TS 4.50). Best format varies: Mermaid (Sonnet), TS contracts (GPT-5), OpenAPI (Haiku, Gemini Pro), C4 (Gemini Flash); all structured formats beat prose on non-frontier models. TS contracts the only format with 100% route coverage and compliance on all six models; Gemini Flash routes 33% (prose) -> 100% (TS). Architecture guidance vs none: +3.34 overall (5.08 -> 8.42). Cost: prose cheapest on Sonnet (433K vs 1,060K Mermaid); Haiku uses more tokens than Sonnet (735K vs 640K) for 1.9 points lower. Demo run rate 100% (Sonnet) to 0% (Gemini Flash). Significance: not tested (n = 3 per cell, stated as exploratory)

Distinguished configurations on weaker models (judge spreads, route coverage) but not on frontier models (Sonnet spread 0.17 within noise; within-condition variance exceeds between-condition on Sonnet). Repeatable: 3 trials/cell; harness and all 93 transcripts released; rounds run sequentially (temporal confound). Judge validated: Sonnet vs GPT-5 r = 0.47-0.60, GPT-5 +0.42 more lenient, no same-family bias; judge vs automated compliance r = 0.21. Limitations stated: underpowered, no significance tests, single system, same author wrote all specs, LLM-judge construct validity

n = 3 per cell, no statistical tests; one system of moderate complexity (~7 components); only proprietary models; all specifications written by the same author; sequential rounds (API load, model updates); LLM judge not validated against humans, possible same-family bias; formats like UML, SysML v2, AADL, Terraform not tested. Future: capability continuum, hybrid formats, larger systems (10+ services), variance reduction, constraint checking in the agent loop, incremental development by a second agent

Data and harness public: github.com/arquicanedo/architecture-as-equalizer (93 transcripts, codebases, specs, judge scores). No pre-registration. Language: TypeScript. Agent is a custom harness, not a commercial agent; model versions without snapshot dates. Inconsistencies: Haiku overall 6.50 in text and Table IX vs 6.55 in Table V; GPT-5-mini 6.72 (Table IX) vs 6.68 (Table V); format effect '10x larger on the smaller model' (p. 2, Sonnet vs Haiku) vs 'up to 14x' (p. 5); paper says specs 'written by the same authors' though single author. Tables extracted with jumbled columns; Table V and VIII values mapped by order and checked against Fig. 2 (p. 8) and text.
